thread:
Jamie: observability alert at 11:03 UTC — p99 /v1/generate ~2.9s, p95 ~1.4s. Streaming stalls +9.2%. Incident bot paged inference-sre.

incident-bot: ALERT: high_latency /v1/generate p99>2s (svc-ingress-prod). Incident INC-452112 created. Paging inference-sre.

Lina: digging in traces — tokenizer/preproc on shard-21 showing huge template_compile times. JSON-mode render and tool-schema assembly look hot. tokenizer p99 ~1.7s, preproc.template_compile p99 ~1.5s.

Mike: logs:
```
[2026-05-12T11:01:58Z] preproc.template.compile latency=1480ms schema_key=user_flow_v10 size=26kb cache_hit=false
[2026-05-12T11:02:02Z] tokenizer.tokenize tokens=602 seq_len=3072 cpu_ms=310
```

Sophia: support reports three customer stream disconnects (delta-ops, prime-qa). Ticket #8522. Marking as customer-impact probably small but visible. Any org list?

Ben: sampling shows affected orgs: delta-ops, prime-qa, sandbox-team. Fraction ~0.9% concentrated on requests with large tool schemas and JSON-mode responses with per-request placeholders.

Lina: hypothesis: heavy synchronous template expansion in hot preproc path + per-request UUID/timestamp interpolation leads to unique cache keys and cache churn. That prevents prefix/KV cache reuse and causes tail latency for streaming (client side timeouts).

Mike: short-term mitigations I can deploy quickly:
- flip runtime flag to enable 'fast_template_fallback' for streaming path
- add schema memoization keyed by content-hash (sha256) with safe TTL and validation
- set preproc.concurrent_compiles throttle to limit CPU contention
- routing: divert schema_size>12kb to dedicated preproc-capacity-1

Jamie: execute runtime flip: /ops runtime-set preproc.fast_template_fallback true --scope streaming

ops-bot: runtime flag `preproc.fast_template_fallback` set true; propagation ~20s.

Lina: propagated; immediate improvement: tokenizer p99 down to ~1.05s, streaming stalls down to +2.6%.

Ben: routing rule applied — matched 0.8% of traffic; rerouted to preproc-capacity-1. Those requests show lower wait times.

Mike: deployed memoization tweak:
```
schema_key = sha256(schema_bytes)
cache.get_or_set(schema_key, compile(schema_bytes), ttl=420)
```
This reduces repeated compiles when schema content is identical.

Sophia: customer update: support ticket #8522 updated — delta-ops and prime-qa had transient disconnects, reconnect succeeded. No data loss. Flagging for PM follow-up.

Jamie: throttled preproc compiles: /ops set preproc.concurrent_compiles=50

ops-bot: config applied: preproc.concurrent_compiles=50

Lina: monitoring — CPU queues decreasing, p99 stabilizing ~0.95s. Good.

Mike: long-term recommendations:
- move expensive template compilation to async preparer with background warming
- sanitize placeholder expansion to maintain stable cache keys (e.g., use deterministic ids)
- tighten service-side limits on tool-schema sizes or add compressed schema support
- implement metric template_cache_hit_rate and alert when low

Jamie: oncall handoff at 11:40 UTC — handing to Lina for monitoring and followups. I'll write the timeline and request a postmortem.

Lina: taking over. Action items assigned:
- validate memoization correctness vs schema updates (use content-hash + versioned TTL)
- gate caching for user-provided schemas until validated
- instrument template_cache_hit_rate and preproc_compile_queue_length
- produce postmortem doc in incidents backlog

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-452112 (High latency for /v1/generate). Mitigations applied; p99 < SLO. Please file postmortem within 72h.

Lina: created postmortem stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-452112-PM — will complete with timeline, root cause, mitigations and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
